title: (A Variant of) Clifford Circuit Synthesis is NP-Complete
abstract: Optimal circuit synthesis is the problem of finding the shortest-depth circuit representation of a given functionality with respect to a pre-specified elementary gate set. This is a central problem in both quantum and classical hardware design. While the classical version is very well understood -- both in terms of heuristics and rigorous hardness assertions -- much less is known about optimal quantum circuit synthesis.   We focus on optimal Clifford circuit synthesis, for which various heuristics are known, e.g. via reduction to 3-SAT. Our main result supplies a matching hardness result: a variant of optimal Clifford synthesis is NP-hard. The proof proceeds in two parts: (i) reduce 3-edge colorability on 3-regular graphs to a circuit synthesis problem that only involves CZ gates, (ii) prove that the availability of additional elementary Clifford gates -- most notably: Hadamard, phase and CNOT -- cannot lead to further improvements of the optimal circuit depth. Our work sharpens the complexity-theoretic understanding of Clifford circuits: simulation and equivalence checking are in P, whereas deciding whether a Clifford unitary admits an implementation within a prescribed depth is NP-complete.
summary: This paper establishes that finding the shortest quantum circuit representation for a given Clifford unitary is NP-hard. It achieves this by reducing the problem to graph edge coloring. Furthermore, it proves that for 3-regular graphs, the optimal circuit depth is determined solely by the number of CZ gates required, regardless of the inclusion of other Clifford gates like Hadamard or CNOT.
main_problem: The paper investigates the computational complexity of optimal quantum circuit synthesis, specifically for Clifford circuits.
main_result: It proves that optimal Clifford circuit synthesis is NP-hard, and furthermore, for 3-regular graphs, the optimal depth using general Clifford gates equals the depth achievable using only CZ gates.
method: The hardness proof uses a reduction from 3-edge colorability on 3-regular graphs to the circuit synthesis problem. The equivalence proof relies on systematically eliminating Hadamard and CNOT gates from the optimal circuit structure.
model_or_system: The model is the quantum circuit implementing a unitary $U_G$ derived from a graph $G$. The analysis focuses on the Clifford group operations using elementary gates like H, CNOT, and CZ.
key_observables: Optimal circuit depth ($	ext{Delem}(U_G)$), edge chromatic number ($\chi'(G)$), and the number of CZ gates ($NCZ$).
important_parameters: The graph $G$ is assumed to be 3-regular, constraining $\chi'(G)$ to $\{3, 4\}$. The analysis often considers circuits of depth $\le 3$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that gates on disjoint qubits can be executed in parallel in a single layer, and the final structural proofs are restricted to 3-regular graphs.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the reduction from 3-regular graph edge coloring to depth-optimal Clifford circuit synthesis, akin to a Karp reduction.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the NP-hardness via reduction from graph coloring. It then proceeds to prove the structural equivalence ($	ext{Delem} = 	ext{DCZ}$) by sequentially simplifying the circuit structure, first eliminating Hadamard gates, then CNOT gates, leaving only CZ gates for 3-regular graphs.
why_interesting: This work provides deep complexity-theoretic bounds on quantum hardware design, showing that even for the relatively simple Clifford group, finding the shortest circuit is computationally hard.
